final_candidates.decision_summary: Supported by positive MSA evolutionary tolerance (z=0.24), highest ESM-1v plausibility (z=1.0), and good backbone compatibility (z=0.74) in a loop region. Most consistently supported candidate despite no direct replication-fitness predictor.
Conservative hydrophobic substitution with excellent structure compatibility (z=0.91) and PLM plausibility, but zero MSA evolutionary signal. Retained with moderate confidence only.

Small-to-small substitution in a flexible stem region, indirectly supported by the tolerated T353I structure score (z=0.74), but never directly screened by MSA or PLM; confidence reflects this uncertainty.

stop_reason.detail: Maximum agent rounds (4) reached; no further tool calls available to screen T353A or other alternatives.

history.rationale: Removing the Thr that primes the N154 glycosylation motif in the E domain I/II hinge region has been associated with altered glycan occupancy and enhanced infectivity in mosquito-adapted Zika lineages.
Glycosylation-adjacent site in domain I/II interface; alanine at T156 mimics circulating ZIKV variants and may enhance receptor-mediated entry fitness. Awaiting evidence.

Only candidate with positive evolutionary tolerance (A freq 0.235 among homologs) plus neutral PLM score and acceptable structure compatibility. Best-supported option for preserving fold while potentially affecting the flexible loop around 154-157.
Consistent support across MSA tolerance, PLM plausibility, and structural compatibility; remains top candidate.
Consistently supported across MSA tolerance, ESM-1v plausibility, and backbone compatibility; loop-region position with multiple supporting dimensions.
Abolishing the N154 glycosylation site (Asn->Gln keeps size/shape) can enhance receptor access and replication in cell culture contexts.
N154 is a known N-linked glycosylation site; altering glycan status can modulate virion maturation and infectivity, but risk to viability is high pending structural/functional evidence.
Q at 154 is rare among homologs (0.029, coverage only 46%) and structure compatibility is poor (ΔlogP=-1.95); conserved N-linked glycosylation-adjacent residue makes this risky.
Low MSA tolerance (z=0.03, app=0.46) and proximity to the N154 glycosylation motif area makes substitution risky for viability.

rejection.reason: Low MSA tolerance (z=0.03, app=0.46) and proximity to the N154 glycosylation motif area makes substitution risky for viability.

history.rationale: A solvent-exposed domain I position tolerant in flavivirus envelopes; conservative hydrophobic change may improve stability without affecting function.
Valine substitution at a mildly variable fusion-loop-proximal position may improve thermostability and hence replication fitness; low prior confidence.
Highest structure compatibility (ΔlogP=+0.59) but zero evolutionary tolerance at an MSA-conserved position, so viability risk offsets structural plausibility.
Strong structural and PLM support with full evolutionary applicability; moderately conserved position caps confidence.
Zero MSA z-score despite good structure score; conservative substitution but no positive evolutionary/functional signal, so moderate confidence only.
Domain III exposed position; hydrophobic substitution may enhance receptor engagement while retaining backbone compatibility.
Domain III tip position; isoleucine substitution is plausible but weakly linked to replication fitness; will re-evaluate against MSA/structure evidence.
No evolutionary tolerance, low PLM plausibility (0.35), and position 353 lies in the stem region; evidence argues against fitness benefit.

rejection.reason: No evolutionary tolerance, low PLM plausibility (0.35), and position 353 lies in the stem region; evidence argues against fitness benefit.

history.rationale: Smaller, PLM-friendlier alternative to T353I in a flexible, structurally tolerated stem position; to be screened next round with PLM/structure/MSA evidence.
Newly added this round; structure evidence for T353I backbone tolerance (E00012) weakly supports, but PLM/MSA screening still pending. Rank tentative until evidence gathered.

Unscreened by PLM/MSA this round; only indirect evidence via the rejected T353I structure score. Confidence lowered to reflect unscreened status; kept as third pick over N154Q because position is not a glycosylation-relevant residue.
